role: Independent ground-truth adjudicator reconciling Reviewer A's (100-claim) and Reviewer B's (84-claim) blind, source-only claim inventories into a single canonical, deduplicated ground-truth list.
inputsDeliberatelyNotUsed: Any Headroom IR, compiled-results, or verification-results file (docs/14-*, 15-*, 16-*, 21-*, or any file with 'compilation', 'verification', or 'compiled' in its name)

This adjudication was performed purely from the two human-simulated reviewers' inventories and the three raw source contracts; no AI-pipeline output was consulted or allowed to influence any matching, materiality, or count decision.

processOverview.step1_ingestion: Read both reviewer inventories (19a, 19b) in full, in original document order, capturing every field (gtClaimId, document, sourceSpan, covenantFamily, propositionType, materiality, shortDescription, requiredQualifiersConditions, quantitativeComponents, dependencies, amendmentOperativeStateRelevance, sourceEvidence) for all 184 source claims (100 + 84).
processOverview.step2_topical_indexing: Grouped both reviewers' claims by underlying contractual subject (e.g., Commitment amount, Availability Period, LTV Table, each individual Event of Default trigger, each fee, each representation, the amendment/restatement recitals chain) to identify candidate correspondences between the two independently-numbered ID spaces (RGT-A-xxx vs RGT-B-xxx).
processOverview.step3_same_claim_test: For each candidate correspondence, applied a strict 'same underlying contractual proposition' test, not a 'same topic' test: two claims were matched (MATCHED_SAME_CLAIM) only if they described the same specific right, obligation, condition, or defined-term content, in the same document context, with the same operative consequence. Claims about the same general subject but a different specific proposition (e.g., the absence of financial *ratio* covenants vs. the absence of general indebtedness/investment covenants; assignment rules vs. participation rules; the LTV pre-funding gate vs. the Fixed Rate definition) were kept as separate, non-matched claims even though they cite overlapping sections or dependencies.
processOverview.step4_granularity_reconciliation: The two reviewers used different granularity conventions in several places: Reviewer A consistently splits a 'baseline (doc-a/doc-b)' state and a 'current (doc-c)' state of the same provision into two separate claim IDs, while Reviewer B sometimes merges a provision's baseline and its amendment-effect delta into one claim (tagged covenantFamily=amendment-effect), and in a few places (RGT-B-004, RGT-B-013, RGT-B-053, RGT-B-058, RGT-B-067, RGT-B-027/028 vs RGT-A-061) one reviewer's single claim corresponds to two or more of the other reviewer's claims covering genuinely distinct sub-propositions bundled together or split apart. In those cases this reconciliation preserved the finer granularity as the canonical unit (i.e., each genuinely distinct sub-proposition became its own canonical claim), and noted in each canonical claim's adjudicationRationale which reviewer's claim ID was reused across more than one canonical entry, so no information from either reviewer's bundling or splitting choice was lost or double-counted as a fabricated extra claim.
processOverview.step5_source_reverification: Where two claims looked similar but might differ in scope, amount, or condition (e.g., whether Section 5.02(g) truly does not exist as a covenant subsection in any of the three documents, and whether its EOD carve-out sentence is truly present verbatim in doc-a/doc-b and truly absent from doc-c), the underlying extracted-text source files were re-read/grepped directly in this session to confirm the reviewers' shared textual claim before treating it as ground truth. This included directly grepping all three source .txt files for the exact carve-out sentence ('a breach by the Borrower of Section 5.02(g) shall not constitute an Event of Default') and for the Section 5.02 negative-covenant subsection headers, confirming: the sentence is present verbatim in doc-a (line 1372) and doc-b (line 1160), absent from doc-c entirely, and Section 5.02 in doc-a runs only through subsection (e) with no (f) or (g).
processOverview.step6_materiality_adjudication: For every MATCHED_SAME_CLAIM pair, the two reviewers' materiality labels were compared. Where they agreed (the large majority of matched claims), the agreed label was carried forward unchanged. Where they disagreed, this reconciliation independently adjudicated the correct label from the source text and the provision's actual operative consequence (not from either reviewer's authority), applying the following rule of thumb: (a) provisions that are standard/boilerplate across most secured credit agreements (e.g., default-interest step-ups, solvency representations, pari passu ranking, a litigation-outcome-contingent judgment default, routine restatement closing-conditions checklists) were generally adjudicated MATERIAL rather than CRITICAL even where one reviewer rated them CRITICAL, unless breach carries an unusually severe or immediate consequence (e.g., an immediate no-cure Event of Default) that independently justifies the higher rating; (b) provisions that are genuinely deal-specific, economically large, or central to this facility's unique BTC-collateralized margin-loan mechanics (the Early Termination Fee formula, the doc-c collateral-release relaxation, the core Commitment/maturity/LTV/interest-rate terms) were adjudicated CRITICAL for consistency with directly parallel claims already rated CRITICAL, even where one reviewer under-rated them; (c) purely definitional/mechanical formula-input claims that feed into a separately-tracked CRITICAL claim (e.g., the Day Count Fraction definitions, which are inputs to the separately-CRITICAL Early Termination Fee) were adjudicated MATERIAL rather than CRITICAL, to avoid double-counting the same underlying risk at CRITICAL twice.
processOverview.step7_singleton_materiality: For claims found in only one reviewer's inventory (A_ONLY or B_ONLY), that reviewer's original materiality label was retained as-is, since no second independent judgment existed to adjudicate against; these labels were nonetheless sanity-checked against the shortDescription/sourceEvidence for internal consistency.
processOverview.step8_special_flagging: Per explicit instruction, the Section 5.02(g)/6.01(d)-referencing carve-out (present verbatim in doc-a and doc-b, silently deleted in doc-c) was represented as two linked canonical claims — one for its presence in doc-a/doc-b (RGT-C-043) and one for its removal in doc-c (RGT-C-044) — both rated CRITICAL, with amendmentOperativeStateRelevance and adjudicationRationale explicitly documenting the deletion, its independent-discovery-by-both-reviewers provenance, and this session's own direct source re-verification, so it can serve as a high-value trust-boundary test case.

matchingOutcomeCounts.arithmeticReconciliation: Of Reviewer A's 100 claims, 73 distinct claims participate in the 75 MATCHED_SAME_CLAIM canonical entries (2 of A's claims — RGT-A-042 and RGT-A-061 — each split across two canonical entries because they bundled two genuinely distinct sub-propositions that this reconciliation kept separate), and the remaining 27 are A_ONLY. Of Reviewer B's 84 claims, 69 distinct claims participate in the 75 MATCHED_SAME_CLAIM canonical entries (5 of B's claims — RGT-B-004, RGT-B-013, RGT-B-053, RGT-B-058, RGT-B-067 — are each reused across 2 or 3 canonical entries because B bundled multiple sub-propositions or a baseline-plus-delta pair into a single claim that this reconciliation split apart), and the remaining 15 are B_ONLY. 73 + 27 = 100 (all of A accounted for); 69 + 15 = 84 (all of B accounted for); 75 + 27 + 15 = 117 canonical claims, correctly falling between the larger single-reviewer list (100) and the naive sum (184).

keyTrustBoundaryClaim.description: Both reviewers independently caught, without being prompted to look for it, that doc-a and doc-b contain an express carve-out ('a breach by the Borrower of Section 5.02(g) shall not constitute an Event of Default') that references a covenant subsection (5.02(g)) which does not actually exist in the Negative Covenants article (which runs only (a) through (e) in all three documents), and that this carve-out sentence is silently deleted in doc-c. This reconciliation independently re-verified both facts directly against the extracted-text source files via grep before finalizing the claims. Both canonical claims are rated CRITICAL and both reviewers, independently, concluded doc-c is the current operative document notwithstanding this deletion — consistent with each other and consistent with this reconciliation's own read of doc-c's Section 1.05 supersession language and recitals.
